newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index crosses 7,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index crosses 7,000 level.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average crossed the 7,000 level for the first time ever Thursday before slipping on profit-taking.

At 1 p.m. EST, the blue-chip Dow was up 33.10 at 6,992.15 after posting a high of 7,000.89 in its first stab above the magic milestone. The rally came one day after the index raced to a record close of 6,961.63.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines by a 2-1 margin on heavy volume of 332 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite Index -- heavily weighted with technology stocks -- was up 9.96 points at 1,368.92, and the American Stock Exchange index was up 1.63 at 594.73.

"You should expect psychological resistance at the 7,000 level," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "From the standpoint of investors who sell on the way up, this is a reminder that the market has been raised another notch and it may be time to rebalance portfolios."
The bond market provided some support for stocks, as the bellwether 30-year Treasury bond rose 7/32, which lowered its yield to 6.69 percent from 6.71 percent on Wednesday.
"The Dow is beginning to struggle a little, but we have a good market today. Breadth is impressive " said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
The market continued to draw strength from the technology sector and bank stocks, which have been responding favourably to the outlook on interest rates.
The Dow romped ahead in what analysts said was the result of simple upward momentum that attracted ever more buyers and kept the averages moving higher.

"At this point, the market is going up because it is going up. People are going in because of the rally and that extends the upward move," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "One of the primary attractions of this market is momentum."
The push past 7,000 came after a morning of hemming and hawing as investors found the millennium mark to be a psychological barrier.
"My guess is that you are seeing foreign trend followers who are mesmerised by the combination of a strong market and a strong dollar," Metz said.
Among the winners, BankAmerica was up 2-1/8 at 120 and Citicorp rose 2-7/8 at 122-3/8.
In the technology sector, Computer Science rose 3-1/4 to 74 and Applied Materials was up 1-1/4 at 53-1/2.
